According to the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Miami, South Florida is experiencing rounds of scattered showers and thunderstorms with localized heavy rainfall and a slight risk of excessive rainfall leading to isolated flash flooding. Breezy to windy conditions with gusts reaching 20 to 28 mph are developing across coastal Miami-Dade County, accompanied by hazardous marine conditions and a high rip current risk along Atlantic waters. These conditions align with Turkey Point's modest storm hazard score and expected peak gusts of 28.6 mph.

articles.title: NWS Forecast Office Miami - South Florida Hazardous Weather Outlook & Marine Conditions
articles.source: National Weather Service Miami - South Florida
articles.snippet: High rainfall rates combined with slow storm motion could result in localized flooding, with increasing northerly winds resulting in gusts in the 20-25 mph range at times and Small Craft Advisory conditions.

articles.title: 7-Day Forecast 25.76N 80.21W - Miami FL
articles.snippet: Showers and thunderstorms likely with breezy to windy conditions persisting into early next week across the coastal Miami metropolitan area.
